families.title: Probabilistic programs: Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and further systems
families.intro: The programs of the Dice, Alea.jl, Roulette and Geni papers, against Dice, Alea.jl and Roulette, and on the programs they take Geni, noDice, Psi, Genfer, SPPL, Pluck, PITA, aspmc, Storm, PRISM, Ace, Merlin, pyAgrum, pgmpy, libDAI and TensorInference.jl. tddlog runs its own encoding of a program's integers (binary, never one-hot) and is asked what the baseline answers: single marginals where the baseline gives single marginals, a distribution's values only where it computes them. Alea.jl's times leave out Julia's start-up and compilation, as its papers time it; the dashed lines add them, and Racket's start-up to Roulette's.

findings.title: Where Alea.jl leads
paras: On multimodal, a circuit of 4 617 random flips at its smallest size, tddlog runs out of memory at that size with each of its three vtrees and Alea.jl answers, in 48 s there. findings.title: The paper's samplers
paras: At the paper's precision the exact answer is closer to the model's than any sampler comes in its runs on GPA (1e-16, which tddlog computes in 43 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁴ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 208 s); tug_of_war (5e-7, which tddlog computes in 1.1 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-5 in 52 s); conjugate_gaussians (5e-6, which tddlog computes in 1.9 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-4 in 71 s); zeroone_w1 (9e-5, which tddlog computes in 0.6 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 2e-1 in 102 s); zeroone_w2 (5e-4, which tddlog computes in 4.2 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁵ samples, comes to 1e-1 in 102 s); coinBias (2e-7, which tddlog computes in 297 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 1e-4 in 31 s); addFun_sum (4e-6, which tddlog computes in 1.5 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's rejection with 10⁶ samples, comes to 7e-4 in 7.3 s); clinicalTrial1 (5e-16, which tddlog computes in 3.5 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁶ samples, comes to 2e-3 in 311 s); clinicalTrial2 (7e-7, which tddlog computes in 0.04 s; the closest sampler, Stan with 10⁷ samples, comes to 1e-4 in 87 s); and addFun_max (3e-7, which tddlog computes in 86 s; the closest sampler, WebPPL's MCMC with 10⁷ samples, comes to 4e-4 in 68 s). paras: tddlog's answers agree with the references everywhere, to 4e+5 relative against Alea.jl and exact references. ProbLog's d-DNNF is wrong on four bit-blasted circuits (clickGraph at 14 bits, by 0.016, pi at 12 bits, by 0.17, wmi_star at None bits, by 0.00022 and wmi_star at None bits, by 6.3e-05), which Ganak's exact count confirms. Dice prints 0 for every answer on 15 bit-blasted circuits, and Alea.jl's discretization is defective in the far tails of a normal, which moves the gene expression program's answer at Figure 2's precision from 1/2 to 0.333 with 5 genes and 0.482 with 20, where the artifact's own runs give 0.4999995 at every number of genes.

setup: Four lab machines: one with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, for the Alea.jl and noDice programs; one with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, for the Dice paper's programs, Roulette's programs and the earlier run of Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs; one with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for the bit-blasted programs; and one with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, for Geni's programs. A run is one job that holds its machine alone. Programs run as independent jobs in lanes, each pinned to one logical CPU on its own physical core, with the machine's memory split between the lanes. In a lane all systems run on an instance back to back, in an order rotated by instance and repetition, so that the systems share the lanes alike.

The release run, all of its parts at one version of tddlog, each part with all of its systems in the same lanes: the arithmetic, sequence and noDice programs (10 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 251 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); the networks, the Dice paper's programs and the loop programs (8 lanes, 15 GB a process, three repetitions, 300 s for the networks and the Dice paper's programs and 600 s for the loop programs, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); Roulette's programs (4 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 16 physical cores and 125 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); the bit-blasted programs for tddlog and Alea.jl (15 lanes, 33 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 20 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-22); and Geni's programs, with ProbLog's d-DNNF timed beside the others (16 lanes, 31 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, on the machine with 36 physical cores and 503 GB of memory, 2026-10-22). Dice, ProbLog's references and the samplers on the bit-blasted programs come from an earlier run (5 lanes, 25 GB a process, three repetitions, 600 s, 2026-10-12) on the same circuits; neither those systems nor the circuits have changed since. Times compare within a run: on the bit-blasted programs the plots show tddlog and Alea.jl, and Dice's times are in the tables only. The plots of all programs put the runs together.

A program with a size runs from small to large, and a system that runs out of time or memory on one size is not run on the larger sizes of that program; the tables mark those `skipped`, and they count as failures. A failure of another kind skips nothing.
A time is the median of the repetitions, a failed repetition counted as longer than any time: of three repetitions, a system must answer in two.

For tddlog and Dice, the wall time of the process: parsing, compiling and answering every query. For Alea.jl, the time the program reports for building the model and computing its answers a second time in the same process, without Julia's compilation, as the papers time it; the process's wall time, with Julia's start-up, loading Alea.jl and compiling its methods, is the dashed line in the plots and the "process" column in the tables. For Roulette, the time the artifact's own `time` reports for building and querying the program; the dashed line adds Racket's start-up and loading.
